A DP-PMP-based energy management architecture for a hybrid wheel loader. The controller exploits repetitive duty cycles to enable real-time optimization of engine start-stop decisions and torque split
Hybrid technologies are considered one of the key solutions for CO

In this context, hybrid technologies have been attracting the attention of researchers and construction machinery manufacturers due to their onboard energy capacity and ease of refueling

Rule-based strategies are simple and have a low computational effort. However, they are typically optimized for a specific mission cycle and do not guarantee the same level of performance in real-worl
In contrast, optimization-based strategies introduce control objectives by defining cost functions to be optimized and thus providing proof of optimality. Dynamic Programming (DP)

Control strategies based on Pontryagin’s Minimum Principle (PMP) are strong candidates for real-time capable control strategies. The application of the Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy (EC
We adapt the DP-PMP approach to off-highway hybrid powertrains and formulate an energy management algorithm.
We present the control architecture, including support functions, to ensure real-time implementation of the developed algorithm.
We evaluate control performance in terms of fuel consumption in both simulation and real-world testing. Additionally, we assess the real-time capability of the controller.

Based on the controller architecture described above, several operational constraints are inherently enforced to ensure robust and real-time operation. As summarized in
Operational Constraints Considered in the Proposed Energy Management Strategy
Battery SOC is constrained within predefined minimum and maximum limits during operation, while the terminal SOC condition is enforced via equivalence factor iteration.
Battery and electric machine power are limited by inverter and hardware constraints and are respected in the control allocation.
ICE start–stop decisions are constrained to discrete vehicle state transitions, which enforces a minimum on/off duration at the state level.
Thermal operation is constrained to the validated operating envelope of the demonstrator; thermal dynamics are not explicitly optimized and are assumed to remain within safe limits.
